brief: A patio bed for tomatoes and the plants that help them grow. A back row of three planters, each three storeys deep, with micro tomatoes in two of them and a pepper in the middle one; a low front row of three one-storey planters with basil, marigold and nasturtium. Fill every planter with soil and plant it.

A salad staircase against a sunny kitchen wall: three rows of three planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so the back row does not shade the front. Lettuce seedlings in the front row, young lettuce in the middle row and full-size romaine at the back. Fill every planter with soil and plant it.

A strawberry tower for a small balcony: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall. Fill every planter with soil and plant strawberries in all seven, with a fruiting plant in the middle one.

A kitchen garden terrace by a sunny back door: three rows of four planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so no row shades the row in front of it. Back row, full-size greens: kale, romaine, chard and bok choy. Middle row, herbs: basil, parsley, mint and chives. Front row: strawberries in two planters, a nasturtium and a marigold. Fill every planter with soil and plant it.

A kitchen garden terrace by a sunny back door: three rows of four planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so no row shades the row in front of it. Back row, full-size greens: kale, romaine, chard and bok choy. Middle row, herbs: basil, parsley, mint and chives. Front row: strawberries in two planters, a nasturtium and a marigold. Fill every planter with soil and plant it. Put the one-storey row nearest the default view and the tall greens farthest from it, and use look to check that every plant is visible from that view.

An FPV drone pit station: a two-storey workbench for a drone pilot, seen from the front. Along the back, a row of six cells two storeys tall: at each end a tower of drawers for spare parts, one drawer on each storey with its front facing the viewer, and between the towers four bins on the top storey, most of them divided, holding M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. In front of the back row, a covered deck one storey high as the work surface. Lay a work pad along the deck with a 5-inch quad on it, a multimeter and a hex driver set at the pad's free end, and the radio and the goggles on the deck beside the pad, one on each side. Put the deck nearest the default view and the back row farthest from it, and use look to check the view.

Build a 3D-printing station from the starter base. At the back, five columns three storeys tall stand in a row along q at r 0 (the starter at q 0, then q 2, 4, 6 and 8), with the cells between them left empty; each column carries rod sockets on its top storey facing the gaps, a spool axle spans each gap, and a 1 kg filament spool hangs on each of the four axles. Each column is topped with a shallow three-compartment bin of M3 screws and nuts. In front, toward the viewer at r 1, a one-storey counter runs from q 0 to q 7 and ties the columns together: covers on q 0 to 3 make the work surface, with a task lamp on the left end, a pencil cup, a hex driver set standing and a hex key set; shallow divided bins on q 4 and q 5 hold screws and nuts; half bases on q 6 and q 7 carry two drawers pulled open toward the viewer, for nozzles, hex keys and tweezers. Cap the open faces, bolt the joints, and leave the meshes clear.

Build a desk command centre that a person sitting in front of it reads at a glance. The viewer is on the side of larger r, so the back of the build is the smallest r. Make two rows. The back row is four full bases, two storeys tall, each with a cover on top, so the tops form a raised deck; stand a 27 inch monitor on that deck, facing the viewer. The front row is four half bases on the ground storey, set in front of the back row, each with a drawer on its cut face so every drawer front faces the viewer, and a half cover on each as a low step. At the left end add two covered bases and put a stack of books on them. At the right end add two bases with divided bins, with pens and markers standing in them, and one covered base carrying a task lamp turned so its head reaches over the bins. On the bench in front of the drawers, far enough out that they can still open, put a keyboard in the middle, a mouse to its right and a phone beyond that, and a mug and a pencil cup to its left. Cap every open face and lock the joints.

An FPV drone pit station for a drone pilot, built in place of the starter base; the viewer is on the side of larger r. Back row at r -1, q 0 to 5, every cell two storeys tall: half-n bases at q 0 and q 5 make two drawer towers, with a drawer on each storey facing the viewer (drawers need half bases on both storeys); full bases at q 1 to 4 carry bins on the top storey, a plain bin at q 1 and divided bins at q 2 to 4, filled with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. In front, a one-storey deck of covered full bases at q 0, r 1 and at q 1 to 4 on r 0 and r 1 is the work surface. Lay a work pad (work-pad) on the deck turned about 30 degrees so it follows the deck's rows, put the 5-inch quad (quad-5in) on the pad, the multimeter and the hex driver set (hexdriver-set) at the pad's free end, the radio on the deck at its left end and the goggles at its right end. Cap the open faces and lock the joints.
